investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-10-11T12:37–12:38Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api layer could not reach the swarm backend ELB at /v1/agents. Because the failure occurs before any agent is provisioned, zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions are unverifiable. This is an eval-detected infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB endpoint that backs POST /v1/agents — was unreachable from the production-api layer at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check calls POST /api/agents, which proxies to that ELB. The gateway returned a 502 bad_gateway with the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning", causing the request to fail before any VM was allocated and before any evidence could be written. The identical error message and near-identical latency (~11 s) across all three sibling checks confirms a single shared upstream dependency failure rather than three independent probe bugs.

Because the failure occurs at the very first step of agent provisioning (the POST /api/agents call to the ELB-fronted swarm endpoint), no evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were ever populated, causing the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state to be fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed service at the redacted us-east-2 endpoint targeted by POST /api/agents — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. This is an upstream infrastructure dependency failure: the production-api layer received a 502 bad_gateway response when attempting to forward the agent provisioning request to the swarm backend, which caused all three remote-agents checks to fail before any agent identity or state data could be collected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure signal, not a confirmed user-traffic incident; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet.

investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Failure: Stale GitHub Actions Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes=682 > max 300)
investigations.summary: The eval check published-observability-snapshot failed because the observability snapshot published at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json is 682 minutes old, exceeding the contract maximum of 300 minutes. This is an isolated eval failure scoped to the snapshot freshness assertion; all sibling public-website checks (public-observability-page, public-models-page, public-marketing-pages) passed, confirming the public web surface itself is reachable and this is not a broad site outage.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 682 minutes (approximately 11.4 hours). The contract requires snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300 (5 hours). The snapshot content is otherwise structurally valid — all required evidence fields are present, source is "github-actions", hasLiveSource is true, and featureCount is 19 — meaning the workflow did run at some point but has since stopped producing fresh output. The most likely operational cause is a GitHub Actions workflow that is disabled, failing silently, rate-limited, or has a broken schedule trigger. No suspect code changes are identified in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges; the root cause is localized to the snapshot publication pipeline, not to the eval runner or contract definitions.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that publishes status.json has not triggered or completed successfully in over 11 hours. This could be due to a disabled, paused, or broken scheduled workflow in the cypher-asi/aura-os repository.
The workflow schedule trigger (cron) may have drifted, been removed, or GitHub Actions may have suspended the schedule due to repository inactivity.
The workflow may be failing mid-run (e.g., a build error, authentication failure, or GitHub Pages deployment error) without updating the published snapshot, causing the age to grow silently.
A GitHub Actions concurrency limit, rate limit, or runner quota exhaustion may be preventing the workflow from executing.

The published snapshot URL (https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json) is reachable and returns a valid payload (generatedAtPresent=true, hasLiveSource=true), so the file exists and is served — the problem is exclusively that it has not been refreshed within the allowed window.
